theme: Rebalancing a line while it is running
title: Rebalancing a Line While It Is Running
isolation: candidate runs as an isolated stdin->stdout subprocess via isorun; the evaluator's internal baseline/reference policies and simulation state stay in the evaluator process
strategies: trivial: keep the given initial boost allocation forever (zero changeover) + uniform buffer split -> reproduces the evaluator's own baseline -> ~0.1 everywhere

greedy: every epoch, dump the whole boost pool onto whichever station has the highest base cycle time THIS epoch (textbook bottleneck-chasing), uniform buffers -> pays a changeover almost every epoch and can even move capacity to a low-effectiveness station; catastrophic on oscillating/drifting bottlenecks

strong: DP-segment the KNOWN full epoch schedule into a handful of static-allocation regimes that only switch when the future payoff beats the changeover cost (anticipates where the bottleneck is headed, not where it is now), then sizes the one-time buffer budget by the imbalance the chosen schedule will actually produce (concentrating buffer at the worst migration/changeover gaps) instead of splitting evenly; evaluated by re-simulating a small menu of (segmentation, buffer-plan) combinations
invalid: malformed answer (wrong row width, over-spent boost pool, too few buffers) -> rejected (0)
